LM Studio has added Z.ai's newly launched GLM-5.3-Flash model to its AI agent platform Bionic, bringing multimodal input, a 1-million-token context window, and pricing significantly lower than GLM-5.2. Details below.

LM Studio acted swiftly to add GLM-5.3-Flash to the Bionic platform

Since its initial announcement in mid-July, LM Studio has continued to expand the models and features supported by its Bionic platform. The platform runs on Mac and Windows and is used for agent-based tasks such as coding, research, and handling documents and files.

LM Studio Bionic can choose to use locally running models, or cloud-based models hosted on U.S. servers, with the latter subject to a strict zero data retention policy.

Shortly after the Bionic platform launch, LM Studio added support for Moonshot AI's Kimi K3. Today, the company officially rolled out cloud support for Z.ai's new GLM-5.3-Flash model. LM Studio says running the model can cost up to 10 times less than GLM-5.2.

LM Studio's announcement comes just hours after the official release of GLM-5.3-Flash. The model had previously been tested anonymously under the codename "Ox Alpha" on OpenCode and OpenRouter, drawing significant attention.

GLM-5.3-Flash is a 320-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model that activates 18 billion parameters per pass, supports image and text input, and features a 1-million-token context window.

Across the benchmarks Z.ai highlighted, GLM-5.3-Flash outperformed GLM-5.2, with overall performance roughly on par with frontier models from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, and DeepSeek.
